Before sleep one makes ablution, lies on the right side and supplicates, entrusting oneself to Allah and affirming His Book and Prophet; dying that night, one dies with faith.
Qunut was recited in Fajr and Maghrib; for a month the Prophet recited it after bowing, invoking Allah against tribes who, despite a treaty, killed about seventy men he sent.
Rising from the last bowing, the Prophet asked Allah to save named weak believers, send famine years on Mudar like Joseph's, forgive Ghifar and save Aslam.
The Prophet seeks victory at Hunain, invokes fire and defeat on the Clans, prays for weak Muslims, against Mudar and named men of Quraish, and answers Jews' death-wish in kind.
Anas says Qunut is before bowing; the Prophet invoked evil on Bani Sulaim for a month, and grieved most for the Qaris whom pagans killed despite a peace pact.
The Prophet prays for the rescue of Aiyyash and Salama bin Hisham and asks Allah to punish Mudar with years of drought like those in Joseph's time.
The Prophet curses certain men, among them Safwan bin Umaiya, Suhail bin Amr and al-Harith bin Hisham, in the morning prayer, and then the verse 'Not for you' comes down.
Asked by Tufail bin Amr to invoke Allah against the Daus, who refused Islam, the Prophet instead asks Allah to guide them and bring them.
The Prophet used to ask Allah for good in this world and in the Hereafter and to be saved from the torment of the Fire.
After bowing in prayer the Prophet cursed certain people and tribes and prayed for named men to be saved, until the verse 'Not for you is the decision' came.
In the Isha prayer the Prophet asked Allah to save Aiyash, Salama, Al-Walid and the weak believers, and to punish the tribe of Mudar with years of famine.
Resting against Aisha, the Prophet asked forgiveness, mercy and to join the highest companions; over the sick he asked the Lord of the people for a cure leaving no disease.
Rising from bowing, the Prophet asked Allah to save Al-Walid bin Al-Walid, Salama bin Hisham, Aiyyash and the weak believers of Mecca, and to send Mudar years like Joseph's.
At bedtime the Prophet lay on his right side with words of surrender, recited the Mu'awwidhat and taught glorifications, and when praying at night asked for light and forgiveness.
The Prophet gave the best plea for forgiveness, said 'In Your name I die and live' at bedtime and taught prayer invocations; invocation should be neither loud nor low.
The Prophet invoked mercy and blessing on Amir at Khaibar, those bringing alms, Jarir sent against Dhul-Khalasa, Anas, a reciter who reminded him of a verse, and Moses.
Avoid rhymed prose in invocation and preach sparingly; ask Allah with determination, not 'if You wish', without growing impatient; the Prophet raised his hands until his armpits showed.
The Prophet prayed for Anas's wealth and children, declared Allah's oneness, Lord of the Throne, in distress, and sought refuge from calamity, an evil end and enemies' gloating.
The Prophet asked Allah to make any abuse of his against a believer a means of bringing that believer near to Him on the Day of Resurrection.
Um Sulaim asked the Prophet to invoke blessing for Anas, his servant, and he asked Allah to increase his wealth and offspring and bless what He gave him.
After ablution the Prophet raised his hands and asked Allah to forgive Ubaid Abi Amir and raise him above many on the Day of Resurrection.
The Prophet's most frequent invocation asked for good in this world and the Hereafter and safety from the Fire; he taught refuge from miserliness, cowardice, old age and worldly affliction.
The Prophet invoked against the confederates, Mudar, Usaiya and those who made him miss Asr at the Trench, returned the Jews' greeting in kind, but prayed for Daus's guidance.
When Jews wished the Prophet death and Aisha cursed them, he urged gentleness, saying he had returned their words and his invocation against them is accepted, theirs not.
After prayer the Prophet said none can withhold what Allah gives or give what He withholds, and told people to seek refuge from calamity, an evil end and bad fate.
In his prayer the Prophet asked Allah to save Aiyash, Salama, Al-Walid and the weak believers, and to afflict Mudar with famine years like Joseph's.
Rising from bowing in the morning prayer the Prophet praised Allah, and in the last rak'a asked Him to curse certain people; Allah revealed that the decision is not his.
The Prophet praised Allah at night as Lord, Light and Truth; he said Allah, Hearing and near, needs no shouting, and taught Abu Bakr an invocation for forgiveness.
The Prophet taught invoking Allah's Name on going to bed, praising Him on waking, and a prayer before relations with one's wife so Satan never harms their child.
In distress the Prophet said there is no god but Allah, the Knowing and Forbearing, Lord of the Mighty Throne, Lord of the heavens and earth.
In distress the Prophet declared none worthy of worship but Allah, the Majestic and Forbearing, Lord of the Tremendous Throne and of the heavens.
In his night prayer the Prophet praised Allah as Keeper and Light of the heavens and earth, affirmed that His word, Paradise and Hell are true, and asked forgiveness.
When asking Allah, be firm and do not say 'if You wish', for no one can compel Him.
No one should say to Allah 'forgive me if You wish', but ask firmly, for Allah does what He wills and none can force Him.
The Prophet taught a bedtime invocation of surrender and trust in Allah, and on the Day of the Clans asked Allah, Revealer of the Book, to defeat and shake them.
In night prayer the Prophet praised Allah as Light and Lord of the heavens and earth, affirmed His promise, Paradise, Hell and the Hour are true, and sought forgiveness.
